title: Episode 2: House of Secrets
premise: A short interactive drama episode about family betrayal, accusations, exile, and mansion-bound secrets, delivered through pre-rendered video scenes with repeated binary story choices.
interaction_model: Tap-to-start, watch fullscreen video scenes, choose between two large on-screen options at key pauses, optionally pause/resume playback, then replay after the ending.
objective: Advance through all six scenes, participate in dramatic decision moments, and reach the episode's final reveal and completion screen.
progression: Linear six-scene progression with five binary choice prompts; choices affect feedback and role-play framing more than story routing, culminating in a replayable episode ending.
theme: Mystery-infused social drama, family conflict, betrayal, hidden money, and secrets inside an ominous mansion.
mood: Melodramatic, moody, gothic, tense, glossy, and episodic.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy mobile visual-novel-style drama, interactive story clips, short-form social conflict narratives, and low-friction tap-based experiences.
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is a linear interactive video story rather than a simulation or action game.
High confidence in the six-scene episodic structure and binary-choice pacing because it is explicitly scripted in code.
Moderate confidence that choices are largely cosmetic because all paths converge to the same next scene in the implementation.
Moderate confidence in story specifics because some narrative detail is inferred from cut-map comments and UI text rather than inspecting the source videos directly.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-friendly interactive visual-story episode titled "Episode 2: House of Secrets." Present it as a fullscreen cinematic experience with a dark gothic-glam UI, a poster-style tap-to-start gate, and six short pre-rendered story scenes that play in sequence as video clips. The story should revolve around family betrayal, suspicious money, accusations, exile from home, and a final move into a mysterious mansion, with a moody soap-opera tone and mystery framing. The player does not control a character directly; instead they watch each scene, then at five dramatic pause points choose between two emotionally charged responses using large thumb-friendly buttons anchored at the bottom of the screen. Keep the structure mostly linear so choices mainly shape the player’s participation and emotional framing rather than causing large branch divergence. Include a small HUD showing the current scene, a progress indicator with six dots, a status badge that changes between warning/success moods, a pause/resume button, quick transition flashes between scenes, short audio cues for start/choice/reveal/pause/resume/completion, looping ambient background audio during playback, and reaction GIF overlays for big decision or reveal beats. End with an "Episode Complete" overlay and a replay button. Use elegant serif display typography with sleek UI text, a neon-magenta-and-violet palette over near-black backgrounds, and overall presentation that feels like a short interactive mansion-drama visual novel made for phones.
